title: Power Automate process mining: Process Intelligence Studio for object-centric models
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, capacity-allocation API and administrator navigation match the sources checked. It distinguishes the planned workspace extension from the documented OCPM preview and does not invent an additional licence requirement. The note about the PowerShell reference needs a citation.

claims.claim: Process Intelligence Studio is a customisable analysis workspace in Power Automate Process Mining.
claims.quote: The new process intelligence experience is the next-generation interface for process analysis in Power Automate Process Mining. It delivers a comprehensive, customizable dashboard for exploring process intelligence insights.

claims.claim: The workspace offers tab-based navigation.
claims.quote: The tab bar organizes your analytical views. It's located at the top of the interface.

claims.claim: Tiles or cards can be arranged in flexible grid layouts.
claims.quote: Customizable layouts where you can arrange, resize, and configure cards

claims.claim: Filters apply across all cards and visualisations on the current tab.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap plans to extend full workspace functionality to OCPM models alongside traditional models.
claims.quote: Object-centric support: Extends full functionality to OCPM models, enabling multi-dimensional analysis of interconnected objects, relationships, and cross-object metrics within the same intuitive interface.

claims.claim: An OCPM event can relate to several objects, including orders, invoices and payments.
claims.quote: With OCPM, each event (for example, Create invoice, Receive goods, Ship order, Record payment) can link to the objects it touched at that moment (for example, Order O1, Invoice I1, Supplier Order SO1, Payment P1).

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: OCPM models are built by ingesting object-centric event logs stored in Azure Data Lake Gen2 or OneLake.
claims.quote: To access OCPM (object-centric process mining) in Power Automate Process Mining, first create a process model by ingesting the object-centric event log (OCEL).

claims.claim: The documented OCPM preview offers only the Process overview tab.
claims.quote: In the preview of this feature, only the Process overview tab is available.

claims.claim: The documented OCPM preview offers only the Default view.
claims.quote: In the preview of this feature, only the Default view is available.

claims.claim: Learn calls the existing analysis interface the process intelligence experience.
claims.quote: The new process intelligence experience is the next-generation interface for process analysis in Power Automate Process Mining.

claims.claim: Object-centric event logs can contain order and invoice identifiers.
claims.quote: each row is an event (with activity and timestamp) and has one or more columns listing the object IDs per object type that the event touched (for example, Order=O2, Invoice=I1)

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[2].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Process mining access follows process and environment permissions.
claims.quote: The process mining capability relies on environment security and Microsoft Dataverse security roles and privileges to grant access to its features in Power Automate.

claims.claim: Learn names the Environment Maker role for creating processes.
claims.quote: You need the Environment Maker role to create, share, and contribute to processes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap describes an analysis workspace rather than announcing a new autonomous automation capability.
claims.quote: It provides a fully customizable analysis environment that combines multiple visualization and analysis components into cohesive, purpose-built workspaces.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Additional licensing specific to this workspace extension has not been published, supporting the unknown licensing model.
claims.quote: Searched: 'object-centric process mining licensing license capacity studio'; 'Process Intelligence Studio licensing'. Read process-advisor-overview licensing, process-mining-studio-overview and object-centric ingestion/overview; no additional extension-specific licence stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Documented Power Automate process mining licensing supplies the product baseline.
claims.quote: Process mining is licensed as part of Microsoft Power Automate. Three Power Automate licenses relate to process mining, and a Power BI license is required for Power BI report customization.

claims.claim: Azure Data Lake storage carries storage costs.
claims.quote: To analyze differences in data storage prices, transaction prices, and storage capacity reservation pricing between accounts that have a flat namespace versus a hierarchical namespace, see Azure Data Lake Storage pricing.

claims.claim: OneLake storage carries storage costs.
claims.quote: Storage charges: The per-GB, per-month cost that's highest for hot storage and lowest for cold storage.

claims.claim: A process-mining-specific capacity-allocation admin UI path is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'ProcessMiningDataStorage admin center allocate process mining capacity'; 'process mining allocate capacity environment admin center'. Read capacity-add-on and programmability-tutorial-allocate-capacity-addons; generic paths do not identify ProcessMiningDataStorage in the UI.

claims.claim: The printed PATCH allocation endpoint, version, currencyAllocations body, ProcessMiningDataStorage currency and allocated count are documented.
claims.quote: PATCH https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/environments/{environmentId}/allocations?api-version=2024-10-01; currencyAllocations | CurrencyAllocationRequestModelV1[]; allocated | integer (int32); currencyType | ExternalCurrencyType; ProcessMiningDataStorage

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center path is Settings > Power Platform settings > Tenant settings > Add-on capacity assignments > Only specific admins.
claims.quote: In the title bar, select the Settings icon. Select Power Platform settings. On the Tenant settings page, select Add-on capacity assignments, and then select Only specific admins.

claims.claim: No setting-specific automation call for restricting add-on capacity assignments was established in Microsoft documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: 'disableCapacityAllocationByEnvironmentAdmins update tenant settings API PowerShell'; 'Power Platform update tenant settings API disableCapacityAllocationByEnvironmentAdmins updateTenantSettings'. Read list-tenantsettings and Set-TenantSettings; no setting-specific write call.

claims.claim: The preview list-tenantsettings documentation defines disableCapacityAllocationByEnvironmentAdmins.
claims.quote: disableCapacityAllocationByEnvironmentAdmins | Boolean | Ability to disable capacity allocation by environment administrators. Default value is false.

claims.claim: The Set-TenantSettings reference does not document a PowerShell call specifically for disableCapacityAllocationByEnvironmentAdmins.
claims.quote: Searched: 'disableCapacityAllocationByEnvironmentAdmins update tenant settings API PowerShell'. Read the entire Set-TenantSettings reference: its example sets WalkMeOptOut and its parameters are RequestBody and ApiVersion; the capacity-allocation property is not present.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powerapps.administration.powershell/set-tenantsettings to sources, and date the note's reference check 'at the time of writing (November 2026)'.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no dedicated environment switch for Process Intelligence Studio or object-centric models.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Process Intelligence Studio turn off disable admin switch'; 'object-centric process mining admin enable setting API'; 'object-centric disable process mining'. Read studio/OCEL pages and settings-features: a general production-ready-preview switch, no dedicated Studio/OCPM switch.

claims.claim: The event log's storage location introduces storage-side access requirements.
claims.quote: all users that have the Owner or Co-Owner role on the process must be attributed: Storage Blob Data Reader or Storage Blob Data Contributor role assigned; Azure Resource Manager Reader role assigned, at minimum.

claims.claim: Power Automate Premium licences contribute process mining capacity.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool up to a total of 100 GB.

claims.claim: The Process Mining add-on contributes additional capacity to the tenant-wide pool.
claims.quote: The Process Mining add-on is a tenant-wide license that's available for the Power Automate Premium license. It offers: An extra 100 GB of process mining capacity to the capacity pool

claims.claim: Process mining capacity can be allocated per environment.
claims.quote: Allocate and deallocate the currencies for the environment. ExternalCurrencyType: The available currency type that can be allocated to an environment. ProcessMiningDataStorage

claims.claim: The add-on allocation programmability tutorial shows using the allocation API through a flow action.
claims.quote: Allocate an add-on using Power Automate flows or Logic Apps. Add a new action to the canvas, searching for "Allocate and deallocate the currencies for the environment". Set the parameters to higher numeric values to perform assignment.

claims.claim: The roadmap identifies business analysts and process owners among the intended workspace users.
claims.quote: Business analysts, process owners, and improvement teams can now build comprehensive views that tell the complete story

controlChecks.governs: Process mining capacity allocated to an environment
